newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on rains, spillover.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on rains, spillover.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled broadly lower in relatively heavy volumes after beneficial rains fell across much of North Dakota, traders said.
Traders said 1/2 to one inch of rain fell in North Dakota over the weekend, covering 70 to 80 percent of the state. The rains helped ease fears of drought conditions in North Dakota.

Spring wheat also drew spillover pressure from KCBT wheat futures, which dropped near their contract lows on the expanding hard red winter wheat harvest in the U.S. Plains and on reports that yields were topping expectations.
MGE spring wheat settled 6-1/2 to nine cents per bushel lower, with July down 8-1/4 cents at $3.72. New crop September spring wheat lost nine cents to close at $3.58-1/4.

Traders said Cargill Investor Services was a seller from the start of Monday's session, shedding at least one million July and one million September bushels. Linnco Futures also sold at least one million bushels each of the July and Sept contracts.
Volume in spring wheat futures was estimated at 35.327 million bushels, the MGE said.
